text:
Done, and it verified cleanly — no LTS incompatibilities existed.

Changes:
- Versions.scala3 = "3.3.8" (publication baseline), Versions.scala3Next = "3.8.4" (verification only).
- crossScalaVersions = Seq(3.3.8, 3.8.4).
- ThisBuild / publish / skip := scalaVersion.value != Versions.scala3.

That last line is the correction the review's sbt mechanics needed. Scala 3 versions share `_3` artifact coordinates, so a cross-publish over both lines attempts to publish ONE artifact twice. Verified directly: `show core/publish/skip` returns false on 3.3.8 and true on 3.8.4.

Verification, both lanes, full suite, under -Werror:
  3.3.8 => 408 tests, 0 failed
  3.8.4 => 408 tests, 0 failed
So nothing in the codebase depended on a post-3.3 language feature; the 3.7.4 pin was excluding LTS consumers for no benefit at all.

githubWorkflowGenerate regenerated .github/workflows/ci.yml; the matrix is now `scala: [3.3.8, 3.8.4]` where it had a single entry. sbt-typelevel narrows the non-primary version to one JDK, which is the right trade — both lines are still verified.

ADR 0001 amended. It named 3.7.4 "its sole publication and verification baseline" and said changing the Scala minor line is an explicit compatibility decision rather than an incidental refresh — so making the change without amending the ADR would have been exactly the drift this epic exists to close. The amendment records why 3.7.4 was a mistake rather than a choice, and why publication is bound to one line.

Not done here, and correctly belonging to P7.6/Phase F: no baseline is CUT. mimaPreviousArtifacts stays empty until a tag exists, so the compatibility gate still checks nothing. B4 only establishes WHICH line a future baseline is published from.
